cursor.note: A seal of `open` is a RECORDED CHOICE NOT TO MEASURE — 'asked for nothing, and said so' — and this voyage made the store say so out loud. The sibling guard already refused sealed -> open (a downgrade). Nothing refused open -> sealed, and because `persist_validation` REPLACES rather than appends, that direction was the more dangerous one: the record that retired the choice left nothing on disk saying the choice was ever made, and the reading that replaced it read as though it had always been there. THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION, and it is the thing worth reading in a year: a detached worktree at HEAD 57bd9cf was handed this voyage's proofs and run — 7 failed, 13 passed. The most legible red was the CLI batch tooth, which watched a three-proof sweep convert three standing readings and print `3 proofs / 3 green / 0 red / isolation netns=3`. A clean sweep over an unannounced conversion IS the defect. TWO THINGS THE VOYAGE LEARNED THAT THE CHART DID NOT KNOW. (1) The CLI teeth landed in test_cli.py, which no decompose berth's writes_to ever named — the split measured the store and missed the surface that calls it. (2) A validate criterion asserted the conversion refusal fires through cairn/tools/base/validation.py's run_proof; reading that function's signature killed it — it takes no isolation argument at all, so it can only ever mint an `open` reading and can never present a measured seal for the conversion guard to refuse. The criterion named an instrument that cannot exist. The validate leg was re-berthed against what the teeth actually prove and the build was NOT moved to satisfy the rewrite. THE ESCAPE IS NOT AMBIENT: converting_because='<why>' rides permanently inside the surviving record's evidence, because a door that replaces has nowhere else to put it. The ordinary path never reaches the guard — `cairn test --seal` reproduces each proof's standing isolation, so sealed -> sealed and open -> open land untouched; only an explicit --netns over a standing `open` gets there, and it now prints an OVERRIDE line naming what it overrode.

window.note: Built and twice-green. SealConversionRefused now sits beside SealDowngradeRefused at the store's one write door, so a measured seal landing over a standing `open` is refused unless `converting_because` rides with it, and the reason lands permanently in the surviving record's evidence because the store REPLACES. The CLI announces the override BEFORE the run when --netns disagrees with a proof's standing reading, reports a refusal on its own line, and carries the batch on. test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped.py runs 10 teeth and test_cli.py runs 10, all green on two consecutive runs. One self-contradicting clause was corrected while here: the file asserted `open` -> sealed was 'the first real seal of a proof that had never been asked', and its own fourth tooth already said nothing standing is not `open`. The reseal ladder is untouched — reseal.py:367 reproduces the standing isolation, so a standing `open` re-runs at `none` and lands open -> open.

THE BEHAVIOUR: call the store's guard predicate with a standing `open` and a measured incoming and assert it refuses, and call it with the three ordinary transitions and assert they still land - either half firing is the watch firing. THE POPULATION: the 54 standing `open` readings counted at arming, against what stands now, minus the conversions that carried a reason; the difference is loss the guard did not catch. Verified capable of firing: handed the pre-build predicate the reading returns fires=true, handed the live one it returns fires=false. `enough` needs 30 days AND a quiet reading, so it cannot clear on the day it was armed. THIS CROSSING NAMES ITS PROOFS: the store guard's teeth live in test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped.py and the surface's teeth in test_cli.py, and both are read since the latest BUILDME.
